title: Nahw Foundations
subtitle: Master the rules of Arabic sentence structure
description: A three-level journey through classical Nahw (Arabic grammar) — from the basic word types and case endings, through verbal sentences and prepositions, to the deeper rules of particles that govern i'rab.

difficulties.label: Beginner
difficulties.description: Word-level foundations — the building blocks of every Arabic sentence

stages.title: Al-Kalimah — Word Types
stages.description: Every Arabic word is one of three types: Ism, Fi'l, or Ḥarf

questions.text: How many types of Kalimah (word) exist in Arabic according to Nahw?
questions.answer: Three (Ism, Fi'l, Ḥarf)

questions.text: What is Al-Ism?
options: A noun — a word referring to a person, place, thing, or idea
A particle with only grammatical meaning
questions.answer: A noun — a word referring to a person, place, thing, or idea

questions.text: What is Al-Fi'l?
options: A verb — a word expressing an action tied to a time
questions.answer: A verb — a word expressing an action tied to a time

questions.text: What is Al-Ḥarf?
options: A particle — has no independent meaning except with other words
questions.answer: A particle — has no independent meaning except with other words

questions.text: Which of these is an example of Al-Ḥarf?
questions.answer: فِي (fī — "in")

stages.title: Signs of Al-Ism
stages.description: How to recognize a noun by its grammatical markers

questions.text: Which of these is a sign that a word is an Ism (noun)?
options: It can be conjugated for past tense
It cannot be preceded by a preposition
questions.answer: It can take Tanwīn

questions.text: Another sign of an Ism is that it can take الـ ("al-"). Which example fits?
options: It can only take الـ in the plural
questions.answer: It can take الـ

questions.text: A word that can follow a Ḥarf al-Jarr (preposition) like فِي or مِنْ is most likely a...
questions.answer: Ism (noun)

questions.text: كِتَابٌ (kitābun) — how do we know this is an Ism?
options: It takes Tanwīn (ـٌ) and can take الـ
questions.answer: It takes Tanwīn (ـٌ) and can take الـ

questions.text: Can an Ism be preceded by the vocative particle يَا (e.g. يَا زَيْدُ)?
options: Yes, this is another sign of an Ism
No, only verbs can follow يَا
Only if the noun is already definite
questions.answer: Yes, this is another sign of an Ism

stages.title: Signs of Al-Fi'l
stages.description: How to recognize a verb by its grammatical markers

questions.text: Which of these is a sign that a word is a Fi'l (verb)?
options: It can take قَدْ before it
It can follow a Ḥarf al-Jarr
questions.answer: It can take قَدْ before it

questions.text: Al-Fi'l al-Muḍāri' (present-tense verb) can be recognized by beginning with which letters?
options: أ ن ي ت (gathered in the word أَنَيْتُ)
questions.answer: أ ن ي ت (gathered in the word أَنَيْتُ)

questions.text: Tā' at-Ta'nīth as-Sākinah (the resting feminine tā', e.g. ذَهَبَتْ) attaching to a word is a sign that the word is...
questions.answer: A Fi'l al-Māḍī (past-tense verb)

questions.text: Sīn at-Tanfīs (the future sīn, e.g. سَيَذْهَبُ) attaching to a word shows it is a...
questions.answer: Fi'l al-Muḍāri' (present/future verb)

questions.text: Can a Fi'l ever take Tanwīn like an Ism does?
options: No — Tanwīn is exclusive to the Ism
Yes, but only in the dual form
questions.answer: No — Tanwīn is exclusive to the Ism

stages.title: Ad-Damā'ir — Personal Pronouns
stages.description: Attached and separate pronouns for I, you, he, she...

questions.text: What does أَنَا (anā) mean?
What does هُوَ (huwa) mean?
questions.answer: "he"

questions.text: What does أَنْتَ (anta) mean, and to whom does it refer?
questions.answer: "you", masculine singular

questions.text: Damā'ir are divided into separate (munfaṣilah) and attached (muttaṣilah). What is a Ḍamīr Muttaṣil?
options: A pronoun that attaches to another word
A pronoun that replaces an entire verb
questions.answer: A pronoun that attaches to another word

questions.text: In رَأَيْتُهُ ("I saw him"), what is ـهُ?
options: A Ḍamīr Muttaṣil (attached pronoun) functioning as Maf'ūl Bih
A verb ending only, with no meaning
questions.answer: A Ḍamīr Muttaṣil (attached pronoun) functioning as Maf'ūl Bih

stages.title: Asmā' al-Ishārah — Demonstratives
stages.description: Pointing words: this, that, these, those

questions.text: هَذَا (hādhā) means...
questions.answer: "this" (masculine)

questions.text: هَذِهِ (hādhihi) means...
questions.answer: "this" (feminine)

questions.text: ذَلِكَ (dhālika) means...
questions.answer: "that" (masculine, far)

questions.text: هَؤُلَاءِ (hā'ulā'i) is used for...
questions.answer: "these" (plural, near)

questions.text: Are Asmā' al-Ishārah (demonstratives) Mu'rab or Mabnī?
questions.answer: Mabnī (their ending does not change)

stages.title: Al-Ism al-Mawṣūl — Relative Pronouns (Intro)
stages.description: An introduction to who/which — connecting words

questions.text: الَّذِي (alladhī) means...
questions.answer: "who/which" (masculine singular)

questions.text: الَّتِي (allatī) means...
questions.answer: "who/which" (feminine singular)

questions.text: What comes after an Ism al-Mawṣūl to complete its meaning?
questions.answer: A descriptive clause (Ṣilah)

questions.text: الَّذِينَ (alladhīna) is used for...
questions.answer: "who/which" (masculine plural)

questions.text: Are Asmā' al-Mawṣūl Mu'rab or Mabnī?
options: They have no ending at all, spoken or written
questions.answer: Mabnī (fixed ending)

stages.title: Ma'rifah wa Nakirah
stages.description: Definite vs indefinite nouns

questions.text: What is An-Nakirah?
questions.answer: An indefinite noun

questions.text: What is Al-Ma'rifah?
questions.answer: A definite noun

questions.text: Which of these makes a noun definite?
questions.answer: Adding الـ ("al-") to it

questions.text: Is a proper name like زَيْدٌ (without "al-") considered Ma'rifah or Nakirah?
options: Ma'rifah (definite), because proper names are inherently definite
It depends on the sentence only
questions.answer: Ma'rifah (definite), because proper names are inherently definite

questions.text: Besides "al-" and proper names, pronouns (like هُوَ) and demonstratives (like هَذَا) are also considered...
options: Definite only when used as a Khabar
questions.answer: Ma'rifah (definite)

stages.title: Alif-Lām — Sun & Moon Letters
stages.description: How the ل of the definite article assimilates or stays audible depending on the following letter

questions.text: What are Al-Ḥurūf ash-Shamsiyyah ("Sun Letters")?
options: Letters that cause the ل of "al-" to assimilate (become silent) and double the following letter
Letters that require a Sukūn on the ل
questions.answer: Letters that cause the ل of "al-" to assimilate (become silent) and double the following letter

questions.text: What are Al-Ḥurūf al-Qamariyyah ("Moon Letters")?
options: Letters where the ل of "al-" is pronounced clearly
questions.answer: Letters where the ل of "al-" is pronounced clearly

questions.text: In الشَّمْسُ (ash-shamsu, "the sun"), ش is a Sun letter — what happens to the ل?
options: The ل is silent and ش is doubled (shaddah)
It changes the meaning of the word
questions.answer: The ل is silent and ش is doubled (shaddah)

questions.text: In الْقَمَرُ (al-qamaru, "the moon"), ق is a Moon letter — what happens to the ل?
options: There is no ل at all
questions.answer: The ل is pronounced clearly

questions.text: Does the Sun/Moon distinction change the WRITTEN spelling of "al-", or only the pronunciation?
options: Only the pronunciation — the spelling ال stays the same in both cases
It removes the ل from writing too
It adds an extra ل when written
questions.answer: Only the pronunciation — the spelling ال stays the same in both cases

stages.title: At-Tadhkīr wa't-Ta'nīth — Gender
stages.description: Masculine and feminine nouns

questions.text: What is the most common sign of a feminine noun (Mu'annath)?
questions.answer: Ending in ة (Tā' Marbūṭah)

questions.text: مُعَلِّمٌ (mu'allimun) — is this masculine or feminine?
questions.answer: Masculine (Mudhakkar)

questions.text: مُعَلِّمَةٌ (mu'allimatun) — is this masculine or feminine?
questions.answer: Feminine (Mu'annath)

questions.text: Are all feminine nouns marked with ة? (e.g. a name like زَيْنَبُ or a word like شَمْسٌ "sun")
options: No — some feminine nouns are feminine by meaning alone, without the letter ة
Yes, but only for human nouns
questions.answer: No — some feminine nouns are feminine by meaning alone, without the letter ة

questions.text: Does the gender of a noun affect the verb or adjective that goes with it?
options: Yes — verbs and adjectives must agree with the noun's gender
No, gender has no effect on agreement
questions.answer: Yes — verbs and adjectives must agree with the noun's gender

stages.title: Al-Ifrād, at-Tathniyah, al-Jam' — Overview
stages.description: Singular, dual, and plural at a glance

questions.text: What is Al-Mufrad?
questions.answer: Singular — referring to one

questions.text: What is Al-Muthannā?
questions.answer: Dual — referring to exactly two

questions.text: What is Al-Jam'?
options: Plural — referring to three or more
questions.answer: Plural — referring to three or more

questions.text: How is Al-Muthannā typically formed from a singular noun?
options: Adding ـَانِ or ـَيْنِ to the end
questions.answer: Adding ـَانِ or ـَيْنِ to the end

questions.text: Arabic grammatically distinguishes between how many categories of number?
questions.answer: Three — Singular, Dual, Plural

stages.title: Al-Muthannā — The Dual in Detail
stages.description: How dual nouns are formed and declined across the three cases

questions.text: How is Al-Muthannā formed when Marfū' (from a singular noun)?
questions.answer: Adding ـَانِ to the end

questions.text: How does the dual ending change when Manṣūb or Majrūr?
options: It stays ـَانِ regardless of case
questions.answer: It changes to ـَيْنِ

questions.text: جَاءَ الطَّالِبَانِ ("The two students came") — what is the i'rāb of الطَّالِبَانِ, and how do we know?
options: Marfū', shown by the ـَانِ ending
questions.answer: Marfū', shown by the ـَانِ ending

questions.text: رَأَيْتُ الطَّالِبَيْنِ ("I saw the two students") — what is the i'rāb of الطَّالِبَيْنِ؟
options: Manṣūb, shown by the ـَيْنِ ending
questions.answer: Manṣūb, shown by the ـَيْنِ ending

questions.text: When a dual noun is Muḍāf (in an iḍāfah), what happens to its final ن؟
questions.answer: The ن is dropped

stages.title: Jam' Sālim — Sound Plurals
stages.description: Regular plurals formed by adding a consistent ending

questions.text: What is Jam' Mudhakkar Sālim (sound masculine plural)?
options: Formed by adding ونَ or ينَ to a masculine singular
questions.answer: Formed by adding ونَ or ينَ to a masculine singular

questions.text: What is Jam' Mu'annath Sālim (sound feminine plural)?
options: Formed by adding ات to a feminine (or some masculine) singular
questions.answer: Formed by adding ات to a feminine (or some masculine) singular

questions.text: مُسْلِمُونَ (Muslimūna) — what is this an example of?
questions.answer: Jam' Mudhakkar Sālim

questions.text: When Manṣūb or Majrūr, the ending of Jam' Mudhakkar Sālim changes from ونَ to...
questions.answer: ينَ

questions.text: مُؤْمِنَاتٌ (Mu'mināt) — what is this an example of?
questions.answer: Jam' Mu'annath Sālim

stages.title: Jam' Taksīr — Broken Plurals (Intro)
stages.description: Irregular plurals formed by changing the word's internal pattern

questions.text: What is Jam' Taksīr (broken plural)?
options: A plural formed by changing the internal structure/pattern of the singular, not just adding an ending
A plural formed only by adding ونَ
A plural formed only by adding ات
questions.answer: A plural formed by changing the internal structure/pattern of the singular, not just adding an ending

questions.text: كِتَابٌ (kitābun, "a book") becomes which plural?
questions.answer: كُتُبٌ (kutubun) — Jam' Taksīr

questions.text: رَجُلٌ (rajulun, "a man") becomes which broken plural?
questions.answer: رِجَالٌ (rijālun)

questions.text: Why is it called "broken" (Taksīr)?
options: Because the word's original singular pattern is reshaped internally, not just extended
Because it refers to broken objects
questions.answer: Because the word's original singular pattern is reshaped internally, not just extended

questions.text: Compared to Jam' Sālim, is Jam' Taksīr more or less common in Arabic?
options: More common — most Arabic plurals are actually broken plurals
It doesn't exist in Classical Arabic
questions.answer: More common — most Arabic plurals are actually broken plurals

stages.title: I'rāb Basics — The Three Ḥarakāt
stages.description: Dammah, Fatḥah, and Kasrah — the three case markers

questions.text: What is Al-I'rāb?
options: The change in a word's ending based on its grammatical role in the sentence
questions.answer: The change in a word's ending based on its grammatical role in the sentence

questions.text: Ar-Raf' (Marfū') is typically marked by which vowel?
questions.answer: Dammah (ـُ)

questions.text: An-Naṣb (Manṣūb) is typically marked by which vowel?
questions.answer: Fatḥah (ـَ)

questions.text: Al-Jarr (Majrūr) is typically marked by which vowel?
questions.answer: Kasrah (ـِ)

questions.text: Which of these three case states applies ONLY to nouns, never to verbs?
options: None — all three apply to both nouns and verbs
questions.answer: Al-Jarr (Majrūr)

stages.title: Mabnī vs Mu'rab (Intro)
stages.description: Words whose ending never changes vs words whose ending changes

questions.text: What is Al-Mu'rab?
options: A word whose ending changes according to its grammatical role
A word whose ending changes only in the plural
questions.answer: A word whose ending changes according to its grammatical role

questions.text: What is Al-Mabnī?
options: A word whose ending stays fixed no matter its grammatical role
A word whose ending changes only when definite
questions.answer: A word whose ending stays fixed no matter its grammatical role

questions.text: Which of these word types is generally Mabnī (fixed)?
questions.answer: Ḥurūf (particles)

questions.text: Are pronouns (Damā'ir) like هُوَ and أَنَا Mabnī or Mu'rab?
options: Mu'rab — their ending changes with case
Sometimes one, sometimes the other, unpredictably
questions.answer: Mabnī — their ending never changes

questions.text: Most ordinary nouns and present-tense verbs in Arabic are...
options: Mabnī only in the dual and plural
questions.answer: Mu'rab (declinable)

stages.title: Al-Mubtada wa'l-Khabar
stages.description: The subject and predicate of a nominal sentence

questions.text: What is Al-Mubtada?
options: The subject of a nominal sentence (Jumlah Ismiyyah), usually first and definite
questions.answer: The subject of a nominal sentence (Jumlah Ismiyyah), usually first and definite

questions.text: What is Al-Khabar?
options: The predicate — it completes the meaning about the Mubtada
questions.answer: The predicate — it completes the meaning about the Mubtada

questions.text: الْبَيْتُ كَبِيرٌ ("The house is big") — what is الْبَيْتُ?
questions.answer: Al-Mubtada

questions.text: In that same sentence, what is كَبِيرٌ?
questions.answer: Al-Khabar

questions.text: What is the default i'rāb of both Al-Mubtada and Al-Khabar?
questions.answer: Both Marfū'

stages.title: Anwā' al-Khabar — Types of Khabar
stages.description: Single-word, prepositional, and sentence predicates

questions.text: What is Khabar Mufrad?
options: A Khabar that is a single word
A Khabar that is a whole sentence
A Khabar made of a preposition
A Khabar made of two coordinated words
questions.answer: A Khabar that is a single word

questions.text: What is Khabar Jumlah?
options: A Khabar that is a complete sentence (nominal or verbal)
A Khabar that is one word
questions.answer: A Khabar that is a complete sentence (nominal or verbal)

questions.text: زَيْدٌ يَكْتُبُ ("Zayd is writing") — what is يَكْتُبُ here?
options: Al-Fā'il only, with no Khabar role
questions.answer: Khabar Jumlah Fi'liyyah (a verbal-sentence predicate)

questions.text: What is Khabar Shibh Jumlah?
options: A Khabar that is a prepositional or adverbial phrase
A Khabar that repeats the Mubtada verbatim
A Khabar that is a question
A Khabar that comes only after Kāna
questions.answer: A Khabar that is a prepositional or adverbial phrase

questions.text: In الْكِتَابُ عَلَى الطَّاوِلَةِ ("The book is on the table"), what serves as the Khabar?
options: عَلَى الطَّاوِلَةِ (the Jār-Majrūr, Khabar Shibh Jumlah)
questions.answer: عَلَى الطَّاوِلَةِ (the Jār-Majrūr, Khabar Shibh Jumlah)

stages.title: Ḥurūf al-'Aṭf — Conjunctions
stages.description: Words that join two nouns, verbs, or sentences together

questions.text: What does وَ (wa) mean as a conjunction?
questions.answer: "and"

questions.text: What does أَوْ (aw) mean as a conjunction?
questions.answer: "or"

questions.text: What does ثُمَّ (thumma) mean as a conjunction?
questions.answer: "then" (with a pause/delay)

questions.text: What does فَ (fa) mean as a conjunction, and how does it differ from ثُمَّ?
options: "and", identical to وَ in every way
questions.answer: "then" (immediately, no delay)

questions.text: When a Ḥarf al-'Aṭf joins two nouns, what happens to the i'rāb of the second noun?
options: It matches (follows) the i'rāb of the first noun
It takes the opposite case of the first noun
questions.answer: It matches (follows) the i'rāb of the first noun

stages.title: Ḥurūf al-Jarr — First Look
stages.description: Meeting the most common prepositions and what they mean

questions.text: What does فِي (fī) mean?
questions.answer: "in/inside"

questions.text: What does مِنْ (min) mean?
questions.answer: "from"

questions.text: What does إِلَى (ilā) mean?
questions.answer: "to/towards"

questions.text: What does عَلَى ('alā) mean?
questions.answer: "on/upon"

questions.text: What is a Ḥarf al-Jarr, in the simplest sense?
options: A short particle that connects to a noun to show a relationship like place, direction, or means
questions.answer: A short particle that connects to a noun to show a relationship like place, direction, or means

stages.title: Al-Jumlah al-Ismiyyah wa'l-Fi'liyyah — Synthesis
stages.description: Bringing it together: recognizing nominal vs verbal sentences

questions.text: What is Al-Jumlah al-Ismiyyah?
options: A sentence that begins with an Ism (noun), typically Mubtada + Khabar
A sentence that begins with a Fi'l
questions.answer: A sentence that begins with an Ism (noun), typically Mubtada + Khabar

questions.text: What is Al-Jumlah al-Fi'liyyah?
options: A sentence that begins with a Fi'l (verb)
A sentence that begins with an Ism
questions.answer: A sentence that begins with a Fi'l (verb)

questions.text: الطَّالِبُ يَكْتُبُ الدَّرْسَ ("The student writes the lesson") — is this Jumlah Ismiyyah or Fi'liyyah, and why?
options: Jumlah Ismiyyah, because it begins with the Ism الطَّالِبُ (even though its Khabar is a verbal sentence)
Jumlah Fi'liyyah, because it contains a verb
Jumlah Fi'liyyah, because the verb comes first
questions.answer: Jumlah Ismiyyah, because it begins with the Ism الطَّالِبُ (even though its Khabar is a verbal sentence)

questions.text: يَكْتُبُ الطَّالِبُ الدَّرْسَ ("The student writes the lesson") — is this Jumlah Ismiyyah or Fi'liyyah?
options: Jumlah Fi'liyyah, because it begins with the verb يَكْتُبُ
questions.answer: Jumlah Fi'liyyah, because it begins with the verb يَكْتُبُ

questions.text: What is the essential difference in classification between these two sentence types?
options: It depends on whether the FIRST word is an Ism or a Fi'l
It depends on the sentence's length
It depends on whether it has a Khabar
It depends on whether it's definite or indefinite
questions.answer: It depends on whether the FIRST word is an Ism or a Fi'l

questions.text: Can a Jumlah Ismiyyah have a Khabar that is itself a Jumlah Fi'liyyah?
options: Yes — as seen in الطَّالِبُ يَكْتُبُ الدَّرْسَ above
Only when the subject is plural
questions.answer: Yes — as seen in الطَّالِبُ يَكْتُبُ الدَّرْسَ above

difficulties.label: Intermediate
difficulties.description: Sentence expansion & governance — fā'il, maf'ūl, and the particles that shape them

stages.title: Al-Fi'l — Tenses Recap
stages.description: Revisiting Māḍī, Muḍāri', and Amr, and the default case of the present verb

questions.text: What are the three tenses (forms) of the Arabic verb (Fi'l)?
questions.answer: Māḍī, Muḍāri', Amr

questions.text: كَتَبَ (kataba — "he wrote") is which tense?
questions.answer: Al-Fi'l al-Māḍī (past)

questions.text: يَكْتُبُ (yaktubu — "he writes/will write") is which tense?
questions.answer: Al-Fi'l al-Muḍāri'

questions.text: اُكْتُبْ (uktub — "write!") is which tense?
questions.answer: Al-Fi'l al-Amr

questions.text: What is the default i'rāb of Al-Fi'l al-Muḍāri' when nothing affects it?
questions.answer: Marfū'

questions.text: Is Al-Fi'l al-Māḍī ever Mu'rab (declinable, changes ending)?
options: Yes, but only in the passive voice
questions.answer: No, it is always Mabnī (fixed)

stages.title: Al-Fā'il — The Doer
stages.description: The subject of a verbal sentence, always Marfū'

questions.text: What is Al-Fā'il?
options: The doer of the action in a verbal sentence, always Marfū'
questions.answer: The doer of the action in a verbal sentence, always Marfū'

questions.text: ذَهَبَ زَيْدٌ ("Zayd went") — what is زَيْدٌ?
questions.answer: Al-Fā'il, Marfū'

questions.text: Must Al-Fā'il always come after the verb in standard word order?
options: Yes — in a Jumlah Fi'liyyah, the verb precedes the Fā'il
No, the Fā'il can freely appear before or after
Word order doesn't matter at all
questions.answer: Yes — in a Jumlah Fi'liyyah, the verb precedes the Fā'il

questions.text: If the Fā'il is feminine, does the verb change?
options: Yes, the verb typically takes a feminine marker (تْ)
Only when the Fā'il is a proper name
questions.answer: Yes, the verb typically takes a feminine marker (تْ)

questions.text: Can the Fā'il be a hidden/implied pronoun (mustatir)?
options: Yes, a hidden pronoun can serve as the Fā'il
questions.answer: Yes, a hidden pronoun can serve as the Fā'il

stages.title: Nā'ib al-Fā'il — The Deputy Subject
stages.description: The passive subject, standing in for the Fā'il

questions.text: What is Nā'ib al-Fā'il?
options: The noun that takes the Fā'il's Marfū' role in a passive sentence, when the doer is not mentioned
questions.answer: The noun that takes the Fā'il's Marfū' role in a passive sentence, when the doer is not mentioned

questions.text: كُتِبَ الدَّرْسُ ("The lesson was written") — what is الدَّرْسُ?
questions.answer: Nā'ib al-Fā'il, Marfū'

questions.text: In the passive voice, what happens to the original Fā'il (the doer)?
questions.answer: It is omitted/not mentioned

questions.text: What happens to the internal vowels of the past-tense verb when it becomes passive, e.g. كَتَبَ → كُتِبَ?
options: First vowel becomes Dammah, the one before last becomes Kasrah
questions.answer: First vowel becomes Dammah, the one before last becomes Kasrah

questions.text: Can a sentence with Nā'ib al-Fā'il be grammatically complete without ever mentioning who did the action?
options: Only if the verb is transitive
questions.answer: Yes

stages.title: Al-Maf'ūl Bih — The Direct Object
stages.description: The noun that receives the action, always Manṣūb

questions.text: What is Al-Maf'ūl Bih?
options: The direct object — receives the action of the verb, Manṣūb
questions.answer: The direct object — receives the action of the verb, Manṣūb

questions.text: كَتَبَ الطَّالِبُ الدَّرْسَ — what is الدَّرْسَ?
questions.answer: Al-Maf'ūl Bih, Manṣūb

questions.text: What is the default i'rāb of Al-Maf'ūl Bih?
questions.answer: Manṣūb

questions.text: Can a verb have more than one Maf'ūl Bih?
options: Yes, some verbs take two objects
questions.answer: Yes, some verbs take two objects

questions.text: Can the Maf'ūl Bih be a pronoun instead of a full noun?
options: Yes, an attached pronoun can serve as the Maf'ūl Bih
questions.answer: Yes, an attached pronoun can serve as the Maf'ūl Bih

stages.title: Al-Fi'l al-Lāzim wa al-Muta'addī
stages.description: Verbs that need an object vs verbs that don't

questions.text: What is Al-Fi'l al-Lāzim?
options: An intransitive verb — does not take a direct object
questions.answer: An intransitive verb — does not take a direct object

questions.text: What is Al-Fi'l al-Muta'addī?
options: A transitive verb — takes a direct object
questions.answer: A transitive verb — takes a direct object

questions.text: ذَهَبَ زَيْدٌ إِلَى الْمَسْجِدِ — is ذَهَبَ Lāzim or Muta'addī, given it needs إِلَى to connect to a place?
options: Lāzim (intransitive) — it needs a preposition, not a direct object, to reach its meaning
Muta'addī, since it has a "place" attached
questions.answer: Lāzim (intransitive) — it needs a preposition, not a direct object, to reach its meaning

questions.text: Can an intransitive (Lāzim) verb be made passive with a Nā'ib al-Fā'il in the normal way?
options: Generally no — passive normally requires a direct object to promote
Yes, in the same way as transitive verbs
questions.answer: Generally no — passive normally requires a direct object to promote

questions.text: كَتَبَ (kataba, "wrote") is Muta'addī. How many objects can it typically take?
options: Two, if followed by a second noun
questions.answer: One

stages.title: Al-Asmā' al-Khamsah — The Five Nouns
stages.description: Nouns declined with letters instead of vowels

questions.text: What are Al-Asmā' al-Khamsah (the Five Nouns)?
options: أَب، أَخ، حَم، فُو، ذُو — declined with letters, not vowels
Nouns that lose their letters in iḍāfah
questions.answer: أَب، أَخ، حَم، فُو، ذُو — declined with letters, not vowels

questions.text: When Marfū', what letter do the Five Nouns take?
questions.answer: و (Wāw)

questions.text: When Manṣūb, what letter do the Five Nouns take?
questions.answer: ا (Alif)

questions.text: When Majrūr, what letter do the Five Nouns take?
questions.answer: ي (Yā')

questions.text: جَاءَ أَبُوكَ ("your father came") — why does أَبُوكَ end in و?
options: Because it is one of the Five Nouns and is Marfū' (Fā'il)
questions.answer: Because it is one of the Five Nouns and is Marfū' (Fā'il)

questions.text: For the Five Nouns to be declined this special way, what condition must be met?
options: They must be Muḍāf to something other than the pronoun ي ("my")
questions.answer: They must be Muḍāf to something other than the pronoun ي ("my")

stages.title: Ḥurūf al-Jarr — Prepositions
stages.description: Particles that govern a noun into Jarr, and their meanings

questions.text: What is the effect of every Ḥarf al-Jarr on the noun that follows it?
questions.answer: It makes the noun Majrūr

questions.text: What does the preposition عَنْ ('an) typically mean?
questions.answer: "about/away from"

questions.text: What does the preposition عَلَى ('alā) typically mean?
questions.answer: "on/upon"

questions.text: بِ (bi) can carry several meanings. Which of these is one of them?
questions.answer: "with/by means of"

questions.text: What does إِلَى (ilā) typically mean?
questions.answer: "to/towards"

questions.text: A Ḥarf al-Jarr together with the noun it governs (Majrūr) is together called...
questions.answer: Jār wa Majrūr

stages.title: Al-Iḍāfah — The Possessive Construction
stages.description: Joining two nouns to show possession or association

questions.text: What is Al-Iḍāfah?
options: Joining two nouns where the second (Muḍāf Ilayh) specifies or owns the first (Muḍāf)
questions.answer: Joining two nouns where the second (Muḍāf Ilayh) specifies or owns the first (Muḍāf)

questions.text: In كِتَابُ الطَّالِبِ, what is كِتَابُ called?
questions.answer: Al-Muḍāf

questions.text: In that same phrase, what is الطَّالِبِ called, and what is its case?
questions.answer: Al-Muḍāf Ilayh, always Majrūr

questions.text: Can Al-Muḍāf take الـ ("al-") or Tanwīn at the same time as being in an iḍāfah?
options: No — it drops Tanwīn and never takes "al-" directly
Only when the Muḍāf Ilayh is indefinite
questions.answer: No — it drops Tanwīn and never takes "al-" directly

questions.text: Does Al-Iḍāfah make the whole phrase definite or indefinite?
options: It typically becomes definite if the Muḍāf Ilayh is definite
It depends only on the Muḍāf, not the Muḍāf Ilayh
It has no effect on definiteness
questions.answer: It typically becomes definite if the Muḍāf Ilayh is definite

stages.title: An-Na't — Adjectives
stages.description: Descriptive words that agree with the noun they modify

questions.text: What is An-Na't?
options: An adjective that describes a noun and agrees with it in case, gender, number, and definiteness
questions.answer: An adjective that describes a noun and agrees with it in case, gender, number, and definiteness

questions.text: الْبَيْتُ الْكَبِيرُ ("the big house") — what is الْكَبِيرُ?
questions.answer: An-Na't (adjective) for الْبَيْتُ

questions.text: In how many things must An-Na't agree with the noun it describes (Al-Man'ūt)?
questions.answer: Case, gender, number, and definiteness

questions.text: رَأَيْتُ رَجُلًا طَوِيلًا ("I saw a tall man") — why is طَوِيلًا Manṣūب?
options: Because it agrees in case with رَجُلًا, which is Manṣūb as Maf'ūl Bih
Because it directly follows the verb
questions.answer: Because it agrees in case with رَجُلًا, which is Manṣūb as Maf'ūl Bih

questions.text: Can An-Na't ever be a full sentence (Jumlah) instead of one word?
options: Yes, when describing an indefinite noun
Only when describing a definite noun
questions.answer: Yes, when describing an indefinite noun

stages.title: Al-'Aṭf — Conjunctions in Depth
stages.description: How coordinated nouns must agree in i'rāb

questions.text: When Ḥarf al-'Aṭf joins two nouns, the second must match the first in what?
questions.answer: I'rāb (case)

questions.text: جَاءَ زَيْدٌ وَخَالِدٌ — what is the i'rāb of خَالِدٌ, and why?
options: Marfū', because it's coordinated onto the Marfū' Fā'il زَيْدٌ
Majrūr, since وَ can also act like a preposition
questions.answer: Marfū', because it's coordinated onto the Marfū' Fā'il زَيْدٌ

questions.text: رَأَيْتُ زَيْدًا وَخَالِدًا — what is the i'rāb of both names, and why?
options: Both Manṣūb, since زَيْدًا is Maf'ūl Bih and خَالِدًا is coordinated onto it
questions.answer: Both Manṣūb, since زَيْدًا is Maf'ūl Bih and خَالِدًا is coordinated onto it

questions.text: بِزَيْدٍ وَخَالِدٍ — what is the i'rāb of both, and why?
options: Both Majrūr, since they follow the Ḥarf al-Jarr بِ
questions.answer: Both Majrūr, since they follow the Ḥarf al-Jarr بِ

questions.text: Can more than two items be coordinated in a single chain with وَ?
options: Yes, the chain can be extended with more items
No, only two at a time
questions.answer: Yes, the chain can be extended with more items

stages.title: At-Tawkīd
stages.description: Emphasis — confirming a noun with nafs, 'ayn, kull, and more

questions.text: What is At-Tawkīd?
options: A word used to emphasize or confirm the noun before it
A word that negates the sentence
questions.answer: A word used to emphasize or confirm the noun before it

questions.text: جَاءَ الأَمِيرُ نَفْسُهُ ("The prince himself came") — what is نَفْسُهُ here?
questions.answer: Tawkīd (emphasis)

questions.text: What is the i'rāb of At-Tawkīd relative to the word it emphasizes?
options: It follows a fixed case, never the word before it
questions.answer: It matches (follows) the same case

questions.text: كُلّ (kull) as a tawkīd word means...
questions.answer: "all/entirety", emphasizing totality

questions.text: Which of these is a word commonly used for At-Tawkīd al-Ma'nawī (emphasis by meaning)?
questions.answer: عَيْن ('ayn)

stages.title: Al-Badal
stages.description: The substitute — a noun that stands in for the one before it

questions.text: What is Al-Badal?
options: A noun that follows another to explain or replace it, taking its i'rāb
questions.answer: A noun that follows another to explain or replace it, taking its i'rāb

questions.text: جَاءَ الْمُعَلِّمُ خَالِدٌ ("The teacher, Khalid, came") — what is خَالِدٌ here?
questions.answer: Badal (substitute) for الْمُعَلِّمُ

questions.text: Must Al-Badal agree with the word before it (Al-Mubdal Minhu) in i'rāb?
options: Yes, it takes the same case
No, it always matches the sentence's default case
questions.answer: Yes, it takes the same case

questions.text: In Badal Ba'ḍ min Kull ("part of the whole"), what does the Badal represent?
options: A part of the original noun
The exact same thing, just renamed
questions.answer: A part of the original noun

questions.text: How does Al-Badal differ from An-Na't (adjective)?
options: Al-Badal can stand alone in place of the first noun with the same meaning; An-Na't only describes it
They are identical in every way
An-Na't can never be dropped, Badal can
Al-Badal must always be a verb
questions.answer: Al-Badal can stand alone in place of the first noun with the same meaning; An-Na't only describes it

stages.title: Kāna wa Akhawātuhā
stages.description: Verbs that raise the subject and put the predicate into naṣb

questions.text: What does كَانَ (kāna) mean, and what effect does it have on a Jumlah Ismiyyah?
options: "was/were" — keeps Ismu Kāna Marfū', makes Khabaru Kāna Manṣūb
questions.answer: "was/were" — keeps Ismu Kāna Marfū', makes Khabaru Kāna Manṣūb

questions.text: كَانَ الطَّقْسُ جَمِيلًا ("The weather was beautiful") — what is الطَّقْسُ called?
questions.answer: Ismu Kāna, Marfū'

questions.text: In that sentence, what is جَمِيلًا called, and what is its case?
questions.answer: Khabaru Kāna, Manṣūb

questions.text: أَصْبَحَ (aṣbaḥa, "became") is a sister of كَانَ. What meaning does it typically add?
questions.answer: "became (in the morning / as a result)"

questions.text: لَيْسَ (laysa, "is not") is a sister of كَانَ. What does it do grammatically?
options: Negates the sentence while still making its Ism Marfū' and Khabar Manṣūb
questions.answer: Negates the sentence while still making its Ism Marfū' and Khabar Manṣūb

stages.title: Inna wa Akhawātuhā
stages.description: Particles that put the mubtada into naṣb

questions.text: What effect does إِنَّ (inna) have when it enters a Jumlah Ismiyyah?
options: Makes the subject (mubtada) manṣūb, keeps the khabar marfū'
questions.answer: Makes the subject (mubtada) manṣūb, keeps the khabar marfū'

questions.text: In إِنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ ("Indeed Allah is Forgiving"), what is اللَّهَ called?
questions.answer: Ismu Inna

questions.text: In that sentence, what is غَفُورٌ called, and what is its case?
options: Khabaru Inna, and it stays Marfū'
Ismu Inna, and it is Manṣūb
Maf'ūl Bih, and it is Manṣūb
questions.answer: Khabaru Inna, and it stays Marfū'

questions.text: Which of these is a "sister" of إِنَّ (same grammatical family)?
questions.answer: لَكِنَّ

questions.text: لَعَلَّ (la'alla), a sister of إِنَّ, means...
questions.answer: "perhaps/hopefully"

questions.text: كَأَنَّ (ka'anna), a sister of إِنَّ, means...
questions.answer: "as if"

stages.title: Al-Ḥāl — The Circumstantial State
stages.description: Describing the state of the subject or object when the action occurs

questions.text: What is Al-Ḥāl?
options: A word describing the STATE of the subject/object at the time of the action, always Manṣūb
A type of adjective for permanent qualities
questions.answer: A word describing the STATE of the subject/object at the time of the action, always Manṣūb

questions.text: جَاءَ زَيْدٌ رَاكِبًا ("Zayd came riding") — what is رَاكِبًا?
options: Al-Ḥāl, Manṣūb, describing Zayd's state while coming
questions.answer: Al-Ḥāl, Manṣūb, describing Zayd's state while coming

questions.text: What is the default i'rāb of Al-Ḥāl?
questions.answer: Manṣūb

questions.text: Must the owner of the Ḥāl (Ṣāḥib al-Ḥāl) typically be definite?
questions.answer: Yes, normally

questions.text: How does Al-Ḥāl differ from An-Na't (adjective)?
options: Al-Ḥāl describes a temporary state during the action; An-Na't describes a lasting quality of the noun
Al-Ḥāl only describes people, An-Na't only describes objects
questions.answer: Al-Ḥāl describes a temporary state during the action; An-Na't describes a lasting quality of the noun

stages.title: At-Tamyīz — Specification
stages.description: Clarifying an ambiguous noun or number, always Manṣūb

questions.text: What is At-Tamyīz?
options: A word that removes ambiguity from a preceding noun or number, always Manṣūb
questions.answer: A word that removes ambiguity from a preceding noun or number, always Manṣūb

questions.text: عِنْدِي عِشْرُونَ كِتَابًا ("I have twenty books") — what is كِتَابًا?
options: At-Tamyīz, Manṣūb, clarifying what "twenty" refers to
questions.answer: At-Tamyīz, Manṣūb, clarifying what "twenty" refers to

questions.text: What is the default i'rāb of At-Tamyīz?
questions.answer: Manṣūb

questions.text: زَيْدٌ أَكْثَرُ مِنْكَ مَالًا ("Zayd has more wealth than you") — what is مَالًا?
options: At-Tamyīz, clarifying in what respect Zayd is "more"
questions.answer: At-Tamyīz, clarifying in what respect Zayd is "more"

questions.text: Is At-Tamyīz usually definite or indefinite?
questions.answer: Indefinite (Nakirah)

stages.title: Al-Maf'ūl al-Muṭlaq — The Cognate Object
stages.description: A verbal noun that reinforces, describes, or counts the action

questions.text: What is Al-Maf'ūl al-Muṭlaq?
options: A verbal noun (maṣdar) from the same root as the verb, used to reinforce, describe, or count the action, always Manṣūb
The direct object of the verb
questions.answer: A verbal noun (maṣdar) from the same root as the verb, used to reinforce, describe, or count the action, always Manṣūb

questions.text: ضَرَبْتُهُ ضَرْبًا ("I hit him, a [proper] hitting") — what is ضَرْبًا?
questions.answer: Al-Maf'ūl al-Muṭlaq, reinforcing the verb

questions.text: ضَرَبْتُهُ ضَرْبًا شَدِيدًا ("I hit him a severe hitting") — what type of Maf'ūl al-Muṭlaq is this?
options: Maf'ūl Muṭlaq of description (describing HOW the action happened)
questions.answer: Maf'ūl Muṭlaq of description (describing HOW the action happened)

questions.text: ضَرَبْتُهُ ضَرْبَتَيْنِ ("I hit him twice") — what type of Maf'ūl al-Muṭlaq is this?
options: Maf'ūl Muṭlaq of counting (how many times)
questions.answer: Maf'ūl Muṭlaq of counting (how many times)

questions.text: What is the default i'rāb of Al-Maf'ūl al-Muṭlaq?
questions.answer: Manṣūb

stages.title: Al-Munādā — The Vocative
stages.description: Calling out to someone with يَا

questions.text: What is Al-Munādā?
options: The noun called out to, usually after يَا
questions.answer: The noun called out to, usually after يَا

questions.text: يَا زَيْدُ (calling a single, definite name) — what is the i'rāb of زَيْدُ?
options: Mabnī on Dammah, in the position of Naṣb
Fully Manṣūb with Fatḥah and Tanwīn
questions.answer: Mabnī on Dammah, in the position of Naṣb

questions.text: What is يَا in يَا زَيْدُ called?
questions.answer: Ḥarf an-Nidā' (the vocative particle)

questions.text: يَا عَبْدَ اللَّهِ ("O 'Abdullah!") — since this Munādā is Muḍāf, what is its i'rāb?
questions.answer: Manṣūb (visibly, with Fatḥah)

questions.text: Besides يَا, are there other (less common) vocative particles in Arabic?
options: Yes, though these are far less common than يَا
No, يَا is the only one ever used
Only when calling someone far away
questions.answer: Yes, though these are far less common than يَا

stages.title: Al-Istifhām — Interrogatives
stages.description: Words used to ask questions

questions.text: هَلْ (hal) is used for what kind of question?
questions.answer: A yes/no question

questions.text: مَنْ (man) as an interrogative means...
questions.answer: "who?"

questions.text: مَا (mā) as an interrogative means...
questions.answer: "what?"

questions.text: أَيْنَ (ayna) as an interrogative means...
questions.answer: "where?"

questions.text: كَمْ (kam) as an interrogative means...
questions.answer: "how many/much?"

questions.text: أَ (the interrogative hamzah) functions similarly to which other particle?
questions.answer: هَلْ, both introduce yes/no questions

stages.title: Ẓuruf az-Zamān wa al-Makān
stages.description: Adverbs of time and place, and their fixed manṣūb case

questions.text: What is Ẓarf az-Zamān?
options: A noun expressing WHEN an action happened
A noun expressing WHERE an action happened
questions.answer: A noun expressing WHEN an action happened

questions.text: What is Ẓarf al-Makān?
options: A noun expressing WHERE an action happened
A noun expressing WHEN an action happened
questions.answer: A noun expressing WHERE an action happened

questions.text: What is the default i'rāb of a Ẓarf functioning as an adverb?
questions.answer: Manṣūb

questions.text: جَلَسْتُ أَمَامَ الْبَيْتِ ("I sat in front of the house") — what is the i'rāb of أَمَامَ?
questions.answer: Manṣūb, as Ẓarf Makān

questions.text: سَافَرْتُ لَيْلًا ("I traveled at night") — what is لَيْلًا?
questions.answer: Ẓarf Zamān, Manṣūb

difficulties.label: Advanced
difficulties.description: Diptotes, weak verbs, deep case theory, and the fuller family of kāna

stages.title: Al-Mamnū' min aṣ-Ṣarf
stages.description: Diptotes — nouns barred from full declension

questions.text: What does Al-Mamnū' min aṣ-Ṣarf mean?
options: A noun barred from taking tanwīn and Kasrah due to specific reasons
A verb that cannot be conjugated
A noun that cannot be used as a Mubtada
questions.answer: A noun barred from taking tanwīn and Kasrah due to specific reasons

questions.text: When Majrūr, what vowel does a Mamnū' min aṣ-Ṣarf noun take instead of Kasrah (with no Tanwīn)?
questions.answer: Fatḥah

questions.text: Which of these is a common reason a proper name becomes Mamnū' min aṣ-Ṣarf?
questions.answer: Being a foreign (non-Arabic) name

questions.text: The plural pattern مَفَاعِل (like مَسَاجِد) is typically...
questions.answer: Mamnū' min aṣ-Ṣarf (Ṣīghat Muntahā al-Jumū')

questions.text: ذَهَبْتُ إِلَى مَسَاجِدَ كَثِيرَةٍ — why does مَسَاجِدَ end in Fatḥah instead of Kasrah, despite following إِلَى?
options: Because it is Mamnū' min aṣ-Ṣarf
Because it is Manṣūb, not Majrūr
questions.answer: Because it is Mamnū' min aṣ-Ṣarf

questions.text: Does a Mamnū' min aṣ-Ṣarf noun become fully Munsarif again if it takes "al-" or is Muḍāf?
options: Yes — it then takes normal Kasrah in Jarr
Only if it is also Muthannā
questions.answer: Yes — it then takes normal Kasrah in Jarr

stages.title: At-Ta'ajjub
stages.description: Constructing exclamations of amazement

questions.text: What is Uslūb at-Ta'ajjub used for?
questions.answer: Expressing amazement/wonder

questions.text: مَا أَجْمَلَ السَّمَاءَ! ("How beautiful the sky is!") — what pattern is used here?
questions.answer: مَا أَفْعَلَ

questions.text: In مَا أَجْمَلَ السَّمَاءَ, what is the i'rāb of السَّمَاءَ?
questions.answer: Manṣūb, as Maf'ūl Bih

questions.text: What is the second common pattern of ta'ajjub, e.g. أَجْمِلْ بِالسَّمَاءِ!?
questions.answer: أَفْعِلْ بِـ

questions.text: In the أَفْعِلْ بِـ pattern, what is the grammatical status of السَّمَاءِ (after بِـ)?
options: Majrūr in form, but Marfū' in position (Fā'il)
Simply Majrūr with no special role
questions.answer: Majrūr in form, but Marfū' in position (Fā'il)

stages.title: Uslūb al-Madḥ wa adh-Dhamm
stages.description: Praise and blame constructions with ni'ma and bi'sa

questions.text: What does نِعْمَ (ni'ma) introduce?
questions.answer: A statement of praise

questions.text: What does بِئْسَ (bi'sa) introduce?
questions.answer: A statement of blame/dispraise

questions.text: In نِعْمَ الرَّجُلُ خَالِدٌ, what is the i'rāb of الرَّجُلُ?
questions.answer: Marfū', as Fā'il of نِعْمَ

questions.text: In that same sentence, what is خَالِدٌ called?
questions.answer: Al-Makhṣūṣ bil-Madḥ (the one specifically praised)

questions.text: Are نِعْمَ and بِئْسَ verbs or particles?
options: Frozen (jāmid) verbs — they don't conjugate for tense
questions.answer: Frozen (jāmid) verbs — they don't conjugate for tense

stages.title: Al-Manqūṣ, al-Maqṣūr, al-Mamdūd
stages.description: Nouns ending in weak letters and how they're declined

questions.text: What is Al-Ism al-Manqūṣ?
options: A noun ending in a fixed ي preceded by Kasrah
questions.answer: A noun ending in a fixed ي preceded by Kasrah

questions.text: What happens to the ي of Al-Ism al-Manqūṣ when Marfū' or Majrūr and indefinite?
options: The ي is dropped, and only Tanwīn on the Kasrah remains (estimated i'rāb)
It stays visible with a Dammah
questions.answer: The ي is dropped, and only Tanwīn on the Kasrah remains (estimated i'rāb)

questions.text: What is Al-Ism al-Maqṣūr?
options: A noun ending in a fixed Alif, whose i'rāb is always estimated (taqdīrī)
A verb in the past tense
questions.answer: A noun ending in a fixed Alif, whose i'rāb is always estimated (taqdīrī)

questions.text: What is Al-Ism al-Mamdūd?
options: A noun ending in a Hamzah preceded by an Alif
questions.answer: A noun ending in a Hamzah preceded by an Alif

questions.text: Does Al-Ism al-Mamdūd decline normally with visible case vowels?
options: Yes, its Hamzah takes visible Dammah/Fatḥah/Kasrah like a regular noun
No, it follows the same pattern as Ism Maqṣūr
questions.answer: Yes, its Hamzah takes visible Dammah/Fatḥah/Kasrah like a regular noun

questions.text: جَاءَ الْقَاضِي ("the judge came") — why is no visible Dammah seen on الْقَاضِي even though it is Marfū' as Fā'il?
options: Because it is Ism Manqūṣ and its i'rāb is estimated (taqdīrī) on the ي
questions.answer: Because it is Ism Manqūṣ and its i'rāb is estimated (taqdīrī) on the ي

stages.title: Kāna wa Akhawātuhā — Extended
stages.description: Ẓalla, bāta, mā zāla, and the rest of Kāna's larger family

questions.text: What does ظَلَّ (ẓalla) mean as a sister of كَانَ?
questions.answer: "remained/continued (during the day)"

questions.text: What does بَاتَ (bāta) mean as a sister of كَانَ?
questions.answer: "spent the night (in a state)"

questions.text: مَا زَالَ (mā zāla) means...
questions.answer: "continued to be / still is"

questions.text: مَا زَالَ الطِّفْلُ نَائِمًا ("The child is still sleeping") — what is the i'rāb of نَائِمًا?
options: Manṣūb, as Khabar of مَا زَالَ
questions.answer: Manṣūb, as Khabar of مَا زَالَ

questions.text: مَا دَامَ (mā dāma) means...
questions.answer: "as long as"

questions.text: Do all of Kāna's sisters function exactly the same grammatically (raf' the ism, naṣb the khabar)?
options: Yes — the whole family shares this same core function
questions.answer: Yes — the whole family shares this same core function

stages.title: Kāda wa Akhawātuhā
stages.description: Verbs of proximity, hope, and beginning

questions.text: What category do كَادَ، أَوْشَكَ، and كَرَبَ belong to?
questions.answer: Af'āl al-Muqārabah (verbs of proximity — "almost")

questions.text: كَادَ الطِّفْلُ يَبْكِي ("The child almost cried") — what is the i'rāb of يَبْكِي as Khabaru Kāda?
options: A verbal sentence (jumlah fi'liyyah) in the position of Naṣb
Simply Manṣūb as a single word
questions.answer: A verbal sentence (jumlah fi'liyyah) in the position of Naṣb

questions.text: What category do عَسَى and حَرَى belong to?
questions.answer: Af'āl ar-Rajā' (verbs of hope — "perhaps/hopefully")

questions.text: What category do شَرَعَ، بَدَأَ، and أَخَذَ belong to when followed by a verb?
questions.answer: Af'āl ash-Shurū' (verbs of beginning — "started to")

questions.text: بَدَأَ الطَّالِبُ يَكْتُبُ ("The student began to write") — what does يَكْتُبُ represent grammatically?
options: Khabaru بَدَأَ, a verbal sentence in the position of Naṣb
questions.answer: Khabaru بَدَأَ, a verbal sentence in the position of Naṣb

questions.text: Do Af'āl al-Muqārabah, ar-Rajā', and ash-Shurū' generally follow the same raf'-ism/naṣb-khabar pattern as كَانَ?
options: Yes, they belong to the same broader family as Kāna wa Akhawātuhā
No, they are entirely unrelated grammatically
Only Af'āl ash-Shurū' follows this pattern
questions.answer: Yes, they belong to the same broader family as Kāna wa Akhawātuhā

stages.title: Al-Ism al-Mawṣūl
stages.description: Relative pronouns and the clauses that follow them

questions.text: What is Al-Ism al-Mawṣūl?
options: A relative pronoun that connects to a following descriptive clause (ṣilah)
questions.answer: A relative pronoun that connects to a following descriptive clause (ṣilah)

questions.text: جَاءَ الَّذِي نَجَحَ ("The one who succeeded came") — what is نَجَحَ called in relation to الَّذِي?
options: Ṣilat al-Mawṣūl (the descriptive clause completing its meaning)
questions.answer: Ṣilat al-Mawṣūl (the descriptive clause completing its meaning)

questions.text: Is Al-Ism al-Mawṣūl (like الَّذِي) Mu'rab or Mabnī?
options: It has no ending at all
It changes only in the dual
questions.answer: Mabnī (its ending never changes)

questions.text: الَّتِي (allatī) refers to which gender?
questions.answer: Feminine singular ("who/which", she)

questions.text: Does Al-Ism al-Mawṣūl require a returning pronoun ('ā'id) in the ṣilah clause that refers back to it?
options: Only when the ṣilah is a Jumlah Ismiyyah
questions.answer: Yes, normally

questions.text: مَنْ and مَا can also function as Asmā' Mawṣūlah (relative pronouns) in addition to their conditional use. What do they mean here?
questions.answer: "the one who" / "that which"

stages.title: Al-Adawāt ash-Sharṭiyyah al-Jāzimah
stages.description: The full range of conditional particles that cause jazm

questions.text: إِنْ (in) among the jāzim conditionals is used for...
questions.answer: General, hypothetical conditions ("if")

questions.text: مَنْ (man) as a jāzim conditional particle is used for...
questions.answer: People — "whoever"

questions.text: مَا and مَهْمَا as jāzim conditional particles are used for...
questions.answer: Things — "whatever"

questions.text: أَيْنَ (ayna) as a jāzim conditional particle is used for...
questions.answer: Place — "wherever"

questions.text: مَتَى (matā) as a jāzim conditional particle is used for...
questions.answer: Time — "whenever"

questions.text: مَنْ يَجْتَهِدْ يَنْجَحْ — how many verbs are affected by jazm here, and why?
options: Both verbs (fi'l ash-shart and jawāb ash-shart), because of the conditional particle مَنْ
Neither, since مَنْ has no effect here
questions.answer: Both verbs (fi'l ash-shart and jawāb ash-shart), because of the conditional particle مَنْ

stages.title: Law wa Lawlā
stages.description: Conditional particles that do NOT cause jazm

questions.text: Does لَوْ (law — "if [hypothetically, unlikely/impossible]") cause jazm on its verbs?
options: No — it does not cause jazm at all
Yes, but only on the first verb
questions.answer: No — it does not cause jazm at all

questions.text: لَوْ اجْتَهَدْتَ لَنَجَحْتَ ("Had you strived, you would have succeeded") — what tense are the verbs in this sentence?
options: Al-Fi'l al-Māḍī (past tense), even though the meaning may be conditional
A mix of Amr and Muḍāri'
questions.answer: Al-Fi'l al-Māḍī (past tense), even though the meaning may be conditional

questions.text: What does لَوْلَا (lawlā) mean?
questions.answer: "were it not for"

questions.text: لَوْلَا اللَّهُ لَهَلَكْنَا ("Were it not for Allah, we would have perished") — what is اللَّهُ called after لَوْلَا?
questions.answer: Mubtada whose khabar is omitted (understood)

questions.text: Does إِذَا (idhā), often meaning "when/if", typically cause jazm like إِنْ does?
options: No, not usually — though it shares a similar conditional meaning
Yes, but only in formal registers
questions.answer: No, not usually — though it shares a similar conditional meaning

stages.title: Al-Fi'l al-Majhūl
stages.description: The passive voice — when the doer is hidden or unknown

questions.text: What is Al-Fi'l al-Majhūl?
options: The passive voice, where the doer (Fā'il) is not mentioned
A verb only used in commands
A verb that has two objects
questions.answer: The passive voice, where the doer (Fā'il) is not mentioned

questions.text: In a passive sentence, what replaces the Fā'il and takes its Marfū' case?
options: Nā'ib al-Fā'il (the deputy subject, usually the original object)
Nothing — passive sentences have no subject
questions.answer: Nā'ib al-Fā'il (the deputy subject, usually the original object)

questions.text: كُتِبَ الدَّرْسُ ("The lesson was written") — what is الدَّرْسُ called, and what is its case?
questions.answer: Nā'ib al-Fā'il, Marfū'

questions.text: How does the internal vowel pattern of a past-tense verb change when made passive, e.g. كَتَبَ → كُتِبَ?
options: The first vowel becomes Dammah and the one before the last becomes Kasrah
It becomes entirely a new word
questions.answer: The first vowel becomes Dammah and the one before the last becomes Kasrah

questions.text: Can a passive sentence still be a full, grammatically complete sentence without a Fā'il?
options: Yes — the Nā'ib al-Fā'il fills that grammatical role
Only if the Nā'ib al-Fā'il is a pronoun
Only if it has an object too
questions.answer: Yes — the Nā'ib al-Fā'il fills that grammatical role

questions.text: If the original sentence had two objects (like with ظَنَّ), what happens to the second object when the verb is made passive?
options: It becomes the Khabar of Nā'ib al-Fā'il and stays Manṣūb
questions.answer: It becomes the Khabar of Nā'ib al-Fā'il and stays Manṣūb

stages.title: Al-Fi'l al-Mu'tal
stages.description: Weak verbs — Mithāl, Ajwaf, and Nāqiṣ

questions.text: What is Al-Fi'l al-Mu'tal?
options: A verb whose root contains one or more weak letters (و، ي، ا)
A verb with a doubled letter
A verb only used in the passive
questions.answer: A verb whose root contains one or more weak letters (و، ي، ا)

questions.text: What is Al-Fi'l al-Mithāl?
options: A weak verb whose FIRST root letter is و or ي
A weak verb whose middle letter is weak
A weak verb whose last letter is weak
A verb with no weak letters
questions.answer: A weak verb whose FIRST root letter is و or ي

questions.text: What is Al-Fi'l al-Ajwaf?
options: A weak verb whose MIDDLE root letter is و or ي
A weak verb whose first letter is weak
A weak verb whose last letter is weak
questions.answer: A weak verb whose MIDDLE root letter is و or ي

questions.text: What is Al-Fi'l an-Nāqiṣ?
options: A weak verb whose LAST root letter is و or ي
A weak verb whose first letter is weak
questions.answer: A weak verb whose LAST root letter is و or ي

questions.text: In Fi'l Muḍāri' from a Nāqiṣ root ending in Alif (like يَدْعُو or يَخْشَى), what happens to that final weak letter when the verb is Majzūm?
questions.answer: It is typically dropped

questions.text: لَمْ يَرْمِ ("he did not throw", from رَمَى) — why does the ي disappear here?
options: Because the verb is Majzūm by لَمْ, and the sign of jazm on a Nāqiṣ verb is dropping the weak letter
questions.answer: Because the verb is Majzūm by لَمْ, and the sign of jazm on a Nāqiṣ verb is dropping the weak letter

stages.title: Al-Ḥāl al-Jumlah
stages.description: When the circumstantial state is a full sentence, not one word

questions.text: Can Al-Ḥāl be an entire sentence (Jumlah) instead of a single word?
options: Yes — it can be a Jumlah Ismiyyah or Fi'liyyah in the position of Naṣb
No, it must always include a Wāw
questions.answer: Yes — it can be a Jumlah Ismiyyah or Fi'liyyah in the position of Naṣb

questions.text: جَاءَ زَيْدٌ وَهُوَ يَضْحَكُ ("Zayd came while he was laughing") — what is وَهُوَ يَضْحَكُ?
options: Jumlah al-Ḥāl (a sentence functioning as Ḥāl), in the position of Naṣb
questions.answer: Jumlah al-Ḥāl (a sentence functioning as Ḥāl), in the position of Naṣb

questions.text: What is the وَ in وَهُوَ يَضْحَكُ commonly called?
questions.answer: Wāw al-Ḥāl

questions.text: Can a Ḥāl-sentence be a Jumlah Fi'liyyah directly with no Wāw, e.g. جَاءَ زَيْدٌ يَضْحَكُ?
options: Yes, this is also valid, especially with a Muḍāri' verb
No, only with an Ismiyyah Ḥāl
Only valid with an implied Wāw
questions.answer: Yes, this is also valid, especially with a Muḍāri' verb

questions.text: In a Jumlah Ismiyyah acting as Ḥāl, what usually links it back to the subject it describes?
questions.answer: A pronoun (rābiṭ) referring back

stages.title: At-Tamyīz al-Malfūẓ wa al-Mulāḥaẓ
stages.description: Explicit tamyīz vs. tamyīz implied by the sentence's meaning

questions.text: What is At-Tamyīz al-Malfūẓ?
options: Tamyīz that clarifies an explicitly-stated ambiguous word
Tamyīz with no noun before it at all
questions.answer: Tamyīz that clarifies an explicitly-stated ambiguous word

questions.text: عِنْدِي عِشْرُونَ كِتَابًا ("I have twenty books") — what is كِتَابًا?
options: Tamyīz al-Malfūẓ, clarifying what "twenty" refers to
questions.answer: Tamyīz al-Malfūẓ, clarifying what "twenty" refers to

questions.text: What is At-Tamyīz al-Mulāḥaẓ?
options: Tamyīz that clarifies the vague subject or object of an entire sentence (implied ambiguity), not a single stated word
Tamyīz that has no grammatical case
questions.answer: Tamyīz that clarifies the vague subject or object of an entire sentence (implied ambiguity), not a single stated word

questions.text: طَابَ زَيْدٌ نَفْسًا ("Zayd became pleasant in himself/spirit") — what is نَفْسًا an example of?
options: Tamyīz al-Mulāḥaẓ, specifying in what respect Zayd became pleasant
questions.answer: Tamyīz al-Mulāḥaẓ, specifying in what respect Zayd became pleasant

questions.text: Does the i'rāb of At-Tamyīz change between these two types (Malfūẓ and Mulāḥaẓ)?
options: Yes, Malfūẓ is Marfū' and Mulāḥaẓ is Manṣūb
Yes, Malfūẓ is Majrūr and Mulāḥaẓ is Marfū'
questions.answer: No — both are still Manṣūb

stages.title: Al-Isnād ilā aḍ-Ḍamā'ir
stages.description: How verb conjugation changes when attached to pronoun subjects

questions.text: What does Al-Isnād ilā aḍ-Ḍamā'ir mean?
options: Attaching a verb to a pronoun subject, changing its conjugated form
Turning a verb into a noun
questions.answer: Attaching a verb to a pronoun subject, changing its conjugated form

questions.text: كَتَبْتُ (katabtu — "I wrote") — what pronoun is attached here, and where is the Fā'il?
options: تُ ("I"), attached and fused as the Fā'il
questions.answer: تُ ("I"), attached and fused as the Fā'il

questions.text: كَتَبُوا (katabū — "they wrote", masc. plural) — what does the وا ending represent?
questions.answer: The attached Fā'il pronoun "they" (masculine plural)

questions.text: In يَكْتُبْنَ (yaktubna — "they write", fem. plural), does the verb's ending change to match the fused Fā'il?
options: Yes — the ending نَ marks the feminine plural fused subject
No, it stays identical to the masculine form
questions.answer: Yes — the ending نَ marks the feminine plural fused subject

questions.text: When a Fi'l is attached to a hidden (mustatir) pronoun like هُوَ in ذَهَبَ, is there still technically a Fā'il?
options: Yes — every verb must have a Fā'il, even if it's not visibly written
Only if the subject is plural
questions.answer: Yes — every verb must have a Fā'il, even if it's not visibly written

questions.text: Does the SAME rule of "every verb needs a Fā'il" apply even to Fi'l al-Amr (command verbs)?
options: Yes — command verbs also have a (often hidden) Fā'il
questions.answer: Yes — command verbs also have a (often hidden) Fā'il

stages.title: Al-Mubtada an-Nakirah
stages.description: When an indefinite noun can validly begin a sentence

questions.text: What is the normal rule for Al-Mubtada regarding definiteness?
questions.answer: It is normally Ma'rifah (definite)

questions.text: Can Al-Mubtada ever be Nakirah (indefinite)?
options: Yes, if it conveys a complete/useful meaning
questions.answer: Yes, if it conveys a complete/useful meaning

questions.text: فِي الْبَيْتِ رَجُلٌ ("In the house is a man") — why is رَجُلٌ, though indefinite, acceptable as Mubtada here?
options: Because the sentence is preceded by a Ẓarf/Jār-Majrūr, giving it a complete/useful meaning
questions.answer: Because the sentence is preceded by a Ẓarf/Jār-Majrūr, giving it a complete/useful meaning

questions.text: In this structure, what actually happens to word order?
options: The Khabar (the Ẓarf/Jār-Majrūr) is fronted before the Nakirah Mubtada
The whole sentence becomes a question
questions.answer: The Khabar (the Ẓarf/Jār-Majrūr) is fronted before the Nakirah Mubtada

questions.text: هَلْ رَجُلٌ فِي الدَّارِ? — does the interrogative هَلْ also help make a Nakirah Mubtada acceptable?
options: Yes, an interrogative context is one of the recognized exceptions
No, هَلْ has no effect on this rule
questions.answer: Yes, an interrogative context is one of the recognized exceptions

stages.title: Al-I'rāb at-Taqdīrī wa al-Maḥallī
stages.description: Estimated and positional case — the deepest layer of i'rāb theory

questions.text: What is Al-I'rāb aẓ-Ẓāhirī?
options: Visible i'rāb — the case vowel is physically seen on the word
I'rāb that cannot be seen or estimated
questions.answer: Visible i'rāb — the case vowel is physically seen on the word

questions.text: What is Al-I'rāb at-Taqdīrī?
options: Estimated i'rāb — the case is understood/assumed but not visibly pronounced
questions.answer: Estimated i'rāb — the case is understood/assumed but not visibly pronounced

questions.text: What is Al-I'rāb al-Maḥallī?
options: Positional i'rāb — assigned to a Mabnī word or a full sentence based on its grammatical ROLE, not any visible marker
I'rāb used only for verbs in the past tense
questions.answer: Positional i'rāb — assigned to a Mabnī word or a full sentence based on its grammatical ROLE, not any visible marker

questions.text: هَذَا كِتَابِي ("This is my book") — what type of i'rāb does هَذَا (Mabnī) have, in the position of Mubtada?
questions.answer: I'rāb Maḥallī (positional) — Raf'

questions.text: A full Jumlah acting as Khabaru Inna would have what kind of i'rāb?
options: I'rāb Maḥallī, in the position of Raf'
It has no relation to i'rāb
questions.answer: I'rāb Maḥallī, in the position of Raf'

questions.text: Why does classical Nahw distinguish between Ẓāhirī, Taqdīrī, and Maḥallī i'rāb at all?
options: Because not every word or sentence can visibly display its case, yet its grammatical role must still be identified
Because Arabic has no consistent grammar
It's purely a stylistic naming convention with no real function
Only Maḥallī actually matters; the others are outdated
questions.answer: Because not every word or sentence can visibly display its case, yet its grammatical role must still be identified

stages.title: Al-Munādā — Deeper Look
stages.description: A deeper look at the vocative and its five categories

questions.text: يَا زَيْدُ ("O Zayd!") — since زَيْدُ is Munādā Mufrad al-'Alam (a single proper name), what is its i'rāb?
options: Mabnī on Dammah, in the position of Naṣb
Fully Manṣūb with Fatḥah and Tanwīn
questions.answer: Mabnī on Dammah, in the position of Naṣb

questions.text: يَا عَبْدَ اللَّهِ ("O 'Abdullah!") — since this Munādā is Muḍāf, what is its i'rāb?
questions.answer: Manṣūb (visibly, with Fatḥah)

questions.text: يَا رَجُلًا ("O [any] man!", addressing an unspecified person) — what is the i'rāb of رَجُلًا here, as Munādā Nakirah Ghayr Maqṣūdah?
options: Manṣūb, since the person addressed is unspecified
questions.answer: Manṣūb, since the person addressed is unspecified

questions.text: يَا رَجُلُ (calling out to a specific man present, though not by name) — what is this category called, and what is its i'rāb?
options: Munādā Nakirah Maqṣūdah — Mabnī on Dammah, like a definite name
questions.answer: Munādā Nakirah Maqṣūdah — Mabnī on Dammah, like a definite name

questions.text: What is the fifth category, Ash-Shabīh bil-Muḍāf, and what is its i'rāb?
options: A Munādā connected to something after it (like a Muḍāf) but not truly a possessive — it is Manṣūb
A Munādā with no connection to anything — Mabnī
The same as Munādā Mufrad al-'Alam
Mabnī on Ḍammah, like other Munādā
questions.answer: A Munādā connected to something after it (like a Muḍāf) but not truly a possessive — it is Manṣūb

stages.title: Al-Mustathnā al-Mufarragh
stages.description: Exception in a negated, incomplete sentence

questions.text: What is Al-Uslūb al-Mufarragh (the "emptied" style) of exception?
options: When the Mustathnā Minhu is entirely absent, and the sentence is negative, so إِلَّا has essentially no grammatical effect
A style where every word is Manṣūb
A style used only in questions
questions.answer: When the Mustathnā Minhu is entirely absent, and the sentence is negative, so إِلَّا has essentially no grammatical effect

questions.text: مَا نَجَحَ إِلَّا خَالِدٌ ("None succeeded except Khalid") — what is the i'rāb of خَالِدٌ, and why?
options: Marfū', as Fā'il — because إِلَّا has no effect in this negated, mufarragh structure
questions.answer: Marfū', as Fā'il — because إِلَّا has no effect in this negated, mufarragh structure

questions.text: مَا رَأَيْتُ إِلَّا خَالِدًا ("I saw no one except Khalid") — what is the i'rāb of خَالِدًا here, and why?
options: Manṣūb, as Maf'ūl Bih — the role it would have had without إِلَّا
questions.answer: Manṣūb, as Maf'ūl Bih — the role it would have had without إِلَّا

questions.text: For Al-Uslūb al-Mufarragh to apply, what condition MUST be met?
options: The sentence must be negative (or interrogative in a negative sense) and the Mustathnā Minhu absent
There must be two separate verbs
It only works with proper names
questions.answer: The sentence must be negative (or interrogative in a negative sense) and the Mustathnā Minhu absent

questions.text: Why is this called "Mufarragh" ("emptied/vacated")?
options: Because the verb is effectively left without its usual object/subject until the Mustathnā fills that empty role
Because the sentence has no verb at all
Because the Mustathnā always comes first
Because the sentence describes an empty space
questions.answer: Because the verb is effectively left without its usual object/subject until the Mustathnā fills that empty role

stages.title: Al-'Aṭf 'alā aḍ-Ḍamīr al-Marfū'
stages.description: Coordinating onto an attached subject pronoun — a fine point of style

questions.text: When coordinating a new noun onto an attached Marfū' pronoun already fused to a verb (e.g. ذَهَبْتُ وَخَالِدٌ), what is generally recommended first?
options: Reinforcing with a separate pronoun (like أَنَا) before the وَ, for clarity and correctness
Repeating the pronoun twice for emphasis
Doubling the verb before the وَ
questions.answer: Reinforcing with a separate pronoun (like أَنَا) before the وَ, for clarity and correctness

questions.text: ذَهَبْتُ أَنَا وَخَالِدٌ ("I and Khalid went") — grammatically, what is خَالِدٌ here?
options: Ma'ṭūf (coordinated) onto the Fā'il, sharing its Marfū' case
questions.answer: Ma'ṭūf (coordinated) onto the Fā'il, sharing its Marfū' case

questions.text: Why do many grammarians prefer inserting a separate pronoun before coordinating onto an attached pronoun?
options: Because coordinating directly onto a fused, hidden-in-form pronoun can sound grammatically weak or ambiguous
Because the fused pronoun changes its vowel otherwise
Because it changes the meaning entirely
Because a fused pronoun cannot take its own emphasis word
questions.answer: Because coordinating directly onto a fused, hidden-in-form pronoun can sound grammatically weak or ambiguous

questions.text: Is the construction ذَهَبْتُ وَخَالِدٌ (without the reinforcing pronoun) considered completely wrong?
options: No — some grammarians allow it, though the reinforced form is more broadly preferred
Yes, but only in Modern Standard Arabic
It's only wrong for feminine subjects
questions.answer: No — some grammarians allow it, though the reinforced form is more broadly preferred

questions.text: This entire discussion is a fine point primarily relevant to which broader topic?
options: Al-'Aṭf (coordination) intersecting with fused pronoun subjects
questions.answer: Al-'Aṭf (coordination) intersecting with fused pronoun subjects

stages.title: Murāja'ah 'Ulyā — Capstone Review
stages.description: The capstone review: analyzing a rich, multi-layered sentence

questions.text: إِنَّ الَّذِي كَادَ يَنْجَحُ لَمْ يَيْأَسْ — identify the role of الَّذِي in this sentence.
options: Ismu Inna, in the position of Naṣb (Mabnī, Maḥallī i'rāb)
questions.answer: Ismu Inna, in the position of Naṣb (Mabnī, Maḥallī i'rāb)

questions.text: In that same sentence, what does كَادَ يَنْجَحُ represent?
options: Ṣilat al-Mawṣūl, describing الَّذِي (كَادَ is Af'āl al-Muqārabah, يَنْجَحُ is its Khabar)
questions.answer: Ṣilat al-Mawṣūl, describing الَّذِي (كَادَ is Af'āl al-Muqārabah, يَنْجَحُ is its Khabar)

questions.text: لَمْ يَيْأَسْ — what is the i'rāb of يَيْأَسْ, and why?
options: Majzūm, because لَمْ is a Ḥarf al-Jazm
Manṣūb, because of a Ḥarf an-Naṣb
questions.answer: Majzūm, because لَمْ is a Ḥarf al-Jazm

questions.text: مَا كَتَبَ إِلَّا مَا يَنْفَعُ النَّاسَ — what construction does إِلَّا مَا يَنْفَعُ represent here?
options: Al-Mustathnā al-Mufarragh, since the sentence is negated with مَا and the Mustathnā Minhu is absent
questions.answer: Al-Mustathnā al-Mufarragh, since the sentence is negated with مَا and the Mustathnā Minhu is absent

questions.text: لَوْلَا الصَّبْرُ لَمَا نَجَحَ أَحَدٌ — what role does الصَّبْرُ play after لَوْلَا?
questions.answer: Mubtada with an omitted (understood) khabar

questions.text: مَا أَجْمَلَ صَبْرَ الَّذِينَ نَجَحُوا! — what uslūb (style) opens this sentence, and what is the i'rāb of صَبْرَ?
options: Uslūb at-Ta'ajjub (مَا أَفْعَلَ); صَبْرَ is Manṣūb as Maf'ūl Bih
A simple question; صَبْرَ is Majrūr
questions.answer: Uslūb at-Ta'ajjub (مَا أَفْعَلَ); صَبْرَ is Manṣūb as Maf'ūl Bih
